svg.title: Trademark and Dispute Defense Around the Portfolio
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-trademark-defense-architecture; chapter number: 11; title: Trademark and Dispute Defense Around the Portfolio; subtitle: Screen before the buy, answer every complaint, read registry terms; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Domain Portfolio Holder; headcount: Single portfolio holder; focus: Hold generic and brandable names without inviting UDRP filings; spokes: role: Pre-Buy Trademark Screen; type: Search check; kpi: Google search, EU trademark and design view, and WIPO global brands database cleared, with no term tied to one major company (live NDDCamp); role: Domain Dispute Counsel; type: External specialist; kpi: A response filed on every complaint; kerosoft.co was lost by default to a $1,330 Forum filing (live NDDCamp, Steven Rinehart); role: ccTLD Terms Review; type: Registry compliance; kpi: Terms read before buying, including .si moral type clauses and Afnic's two-week reply deadline (domainsherpa); role: gTLD String Vetting; type: Extension strategy; kpi: String run through the Name Collision Observatory early, never relied on alone (ICANN); caption: A typical UDRP lands in about 60 days versus 259 for an ACPA final judgment, and a complainant's run costs about $5,000 in lawyer fees plus a $1,500 filing fee.; assumptions note: Timelines and costs are as reported by Doug Isenberg and NDDCamp panelists; Steven Rinehart separately quotes 34 to 44 days for a UDRP.; note: Sources GigaLaw with Doug Isenberg (GI9Us2WWsAo @ 00:06:31), live NDDCamp (PdwE4T9wmMo @ 00:04:24 and 00:33:12), Steven Rinehart (BL9pY270FpM @ 00:02:37), domainsherpa (4lvZ-LZJ3Sc @ 00:19:19), ICANN (ubAwLfPKk6s @ 00:02:48).
